summary.tone: Restrained, confident product teaser: dark grainy draped backdrops, recreated UI in macro close-ups, no voice-over, ending on a minimalist mono-type feature roll and a release year rather than an explicit call to action.

signature_moments.description: The emoji-grid selection steps onto a microphone emoji, the grid blurs away and the tile shrinks into a circular dictation button that stretches into a voice-input pill with a live waveform, which leads straight into the typed AI prompt.
signature_moments.why_premium: One continuous object morph links two unrelated features (emoji picker and voice/AI input) without a cut, which reads as custom-built motion rather than stitched screen captures.

signature_moments.description: Opens on an extreme, edge-cropped macro of the search bar with a blinking caret drifting over a grainy fabric backdrop, then pulls back fast to the normal-size launcher.
signature_moments.why_premium: Treating the most familiar UI element as a hero object at huge scale creates intrigue with almost no content, and the pull-back gives a clean reveal of scale.

signature_moments.description: A mono-type end card cycles 'NEW' + seven feature names every half second, then closes the gap to 'NEW RAYCAST', adds 'COMING 2026' in italic and resolves to the logo.
signature_moments.why_premium: It recaps every feature shown in a few seconds with pure typography and restraint, giving the visual demo a verbal label without voice-over.

hook.evidence: Macro close-up of the search bar with blinking caret and a fast pull-back is intriguing and on-brand, but it states no claim or benefit; it relies on curiosity alone.

clarity.evidence: Each feature is shown as a short, legible UI moment (clipboard, hotkeys, emoji, voice, AI chat), but with no voice-over or captions during the demo the feature names only appear in the end-card roll; several steps (s009, s010) pass in about 2 s each.

ui_showcase.evidence: Recreated UI is crisp and art-directed: typed queries, action menus, hotkey dialog with success state, staggered lists, masked scrolls and tool-call rows revealed through gradient masks, all at large crops.

motion_polish.evidence: Continuous reframes and morphs instead of cuts (tile to mic button to pill, list to emoji grid inside one panel mask), consistent eased camera drift and well-timed reveals across shots.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors only, not heard: a music track at 129.2 BPM with beats detected only up to about 24.7 s (none during most of the s011-s012 end section), integrated loudness -13.2 LUFS, no SFX candidates detected and no speech. The end-card word swaps at roughly 0.5 s are close to the beat period but sync cannot be confirmed.

vo_script_quality.evidence: No voice-over: the anchors transcript has no words.

brand_consistency.evidence: One dark, grainy draped-fabric backdrop, one UI sans face and the native Raycast dark UI throughout, closing on a mono-type card and the logo.

works_muted.evidence: Nothing depends on audio (no voice-over, no SFX detected); the demo reads visually and the end card names the features, though their purpose is left for viewers to infer.

overall.evidence: Best-in-class UI craft and motion for a teaser, held back by limited explanation of what each feature does and by no explicit call to action beyond 'COMING 2026'.

localization_friendliness.notes: No voice-over, so no dubbing is needed; but all UI strings in the demo and the end-card feature roll are baked into the picture, so a localized version would need the UI recreations and the end card re-rendered.
